speaker: m_ana
text: Mom's seventy-eight and alone in Queens. She mixes up her pills, she almost wired money to someone pretending to be Marco last week, and last Thursday nobody went to see her because Marco and I each thought the other was going.

speaker: m_ana
text: Carmen. Carmen Reyes. Spanish, siempre. She understands English, but when she's tired it's all español.

speaker: m_ana
text: My brother Marco, and my sister Lucía, but Lucía's in Boston, so she handles the Medicare paperwork and orders the groceries online. Mrs. Ortiz next door checks on her sometimes.

speaker: m_ana
text: She won't use an app, she'll answer the phone. It's a flip phone. Me, Marco, Lucía, we all have smartphones, the app is fine.

speaker: m_ana
text: Eliquis twice a day, lisinopril, metformin and atorvastatin. Four. Dr. Lee at Elmhurst bumped the lisinopril to ten in October. She has the organizer, mañana y noche.

speaker: m_ana
text: Last week somebody called crying, pretending to be Marco, asking for two thousand dollars. She almost wired it. Gracias a Dios she called me first.

speaker: m_ana
text: I go Mondays, Wednesdays and Sundays after school. Marco does Tuesdays, Thursdays, Fridays and Saturdays during the day and refills the organizer on Fridays, he works nights. Last Thursday nobody went, he thought it was me.

speaker: m_ana
text: She still shops at the bodega on 37th but she can't carry bags up three floors. The super has keys. Bills are on autopay, Lucía watches those.

speaker: m_ana
text: Don't call her late. She'll tell you herself, but después de las nueve y media, no.

speaker: m_ana
text: Yes, call me anytime. Marco said it's fine too. Lucía prefers texts, no calls.
